topics.title: Problem & motivation
topics.prompt: What problem are you solving? Why does this project exist? Why now?
topics.body: GNU Stow is powerful but CLI-only: you memorize flags, run it per package group, and get no overview of what is stowed, conflicted, or missing. andre exists to make routine dotfiles management faster and less error-prone by giving stow a terminal UI. Select groups and packages visually, toggle options (dry-run, verbosity, adopt, no-folding), execute with live feedback, adopt existing files into packages, unstow interactively, and edit the config in place — all without leaving the keyboard workflow stow users already have.

topics.title: Who is it for?
topics.prompt: Primary users or consumers. Who is explicitly NOT the audience?
topics.body: Developers, hobbyists, and power users who keep their dotfiles in version control and already drive GNU Stow by hand, on macOS or Linux, and are comfortable in a terminal. Explicitly NOT the audience: non-technical users, anyone not using stow (chezmoi/yadm users stay with their tools), GUI-only users, and anyone wanting cloud sync or remote/multi-machine management.

topics.title: Rough capabilities
topics.prompt: What might it do? Brainstorm features or behaviors — rough is fine, no ordering yet.
topics.body: Multi-group stow config (e.g. `~`, `~/.config`); interactive group + package selection with smart pre-selection; live settings toggles from any screen; in-TUI config editor (add/remove/edit groups, change global defaults); guided adoption (import existing target files into a new package); interactive unstow (unlink symlinks per file); headless `--yolo` mode for scripts/automation; config auto-discovery (`$PWD`, `~/dotfiles/`, `~/.dotfiles/`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`); real stow status display (stowed/unstowed/conflicted/missing); theme cycling; debug logging.

topics.title: Constraints
topics.prompt: Time, budget, stack preferences, platform, team size, legal, or technical limits.
topics.body: Rust workspace (andre-core logic crate + andre TUI crate); ratatui + crossterm + tokio; requires GNU Stow installed on the host; local-only — no network, no daemon; targets macOS and Linux; MIT licensed; solo developer; the `andre.yml` config format is frozen (no breaking changes) after v1.0.

topics.title: Inspiration & references
topics.prompt: Similar products, links, repos, or experiences you want to learn from or avoid.
topics.body: GNU Stow itself (the underlying tool). Sibling project lazybrew (a TUI for Homebrew) shares the architecture and conventions. Other dotfiles managers (chezmoi, yadm) take a different approach — andre deliberately stays a thin stow wrapper rather than a rival manager.

topics.title: Unknowns & open questions
topics.prompt: What don't you know yet? What needs research or a spike?
topics.body: Exact v1.0 release criteria (how much real-world battle-testing is enough). Linux smoke-test coverage is currently manual. The TUI integration test `test_add_group_then_save_persists` depends on the real host home dir and fails on minimal Linux CI images — needs a test-isolation fix. Whether to expand scope beyond stow post-1.0 is undecided.

topics.title: What success looks like
topics.prompt: How will you know this worked? Vague is OK — we'll sharpen this in the charter.
topics.body: andre is a reliable daily-driver TUI for stow on macOS + Linux. v1.0 ships with a frozen, documented `andre.yml` format. CI is green on both platforms with coverage thresholds held (andre-core >= 88%, TUI >= 38%), clippy clean, and the Homebrew install path works end to end.

topics.title: Explicit non-starters
topics.prompt: What are you probably NOT doing in v1? Ideas to park, not reject forever.
topics.body: No GUI — terminal/TUI only. No cloud sync, remote, or multi-machine management. Not a replacement for GNU Stow (a wrapper). No always-on automation daemon. No Windows support. No breaking `andre.yml` changes after v1.0.
